In the 5 months I've owned my (first) bike I had so many close calls it's not even funny. It's to a point where when my rear tire locks up and I'm coming up fast on an object, curve, or whatever I don't even pause or panic I just instantly know what to do to fix the problem. I still get a little adrenaline, but I just laugh it off and keep going. I've also had quite a few people passing each other coming toward me filling both lanes, mine and theirs. I don't slow down, I just hug the edge of the road and it all works out.

Is it normal not to freak out when stuff like this happens?
Has anyone else gotten used to close calls?

Honestly I have the freak out after it happens... which is a good thing, right? Better than panic during the moment.

Like Lee Parks said in his book Total Control (paraphrased) "Take after stand-up comedians. When something unexpected happens, pretend like you wanted it to"

Don't get cocky. I'd say overconfidence is just as dangerous as inexperience, and at 5 months you're still pretty inexperienced, admit it or not.

Go do a track day. I've said it before and I'll say it again, I learned more in my first track session about the capabilities of my bike (and myself) than I did in my first couple years of street riding. You haven't lived till you've spun up your rear tire deep in a corner - heh.

Wow, I haven't had anything as bad as that, or at least as frequently.

I try to watch out for what other drivers are about to do. The most common thing that happens to me is cars changing lanes without checking their blindspot, or exiting or continuing round roundabouts when in the wrong lane. Fortunately both of these mistakes can be predicted and worked around, but it still makes me so angry to see a lorry careen across the lane I would've been in.

If your locking up the rear brake all the time then you need to get somewhere where you can learn to rely more on your front brakes. Rear brake lockups and pitch you. This is rider error. Find balance between your front and rear and learn not to panic lock your rears. Experience and a focus on learning to rely more on your fronts will solve the problem.

I've been riding since I was 5, I'm 27 now, and I'm still not used to it. It doesn't have the same grip on my as it used to, but after real close ones, I still pull over afterwards.

If you've had that many close calls in such a short time, you need to start reflecting and implementing more. No matter how long you've ridden, it only takes one time to take it all away.
